 Coby White, Sion James, Grayson Allen, Naz Reid and Ryan Kalkbrenner will start Monday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 The Hornets will not have Brandon Miller for Monday’s game, opening up a spot in the starting lineup. The void will be filled by James, whose presence should allow White to spend more time playing off the ball. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) will be re-evaluated in four weeks. 
 Knueppel strained his left hamstring before training camp and did not make his season debut until Wednesday. Unfortunately, he left after six minutes and has been diagnosed with another strain of the same hamstring. Knueppel’s absence should push Sion James back into the starting lineup, but he offers limited fantasy value as a streamer. 
 Dennis Schröder 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #17 
 Dennis Schröder (thigh) is questionable to play against the Celtics on Friday. 
 Schröder could miss a game for the first time this season. Coby White is healthy, but he’s on a strict minutes restriction. Rookie Christian Anderson has been assigned to the G League, so Sion James, who is already starting, would likely operate as the backup point guard if Schröder is out. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (leg) will not return to Wednesday’s game against the Nets. 
 Making his first appearance of the season after straining his left hamstring before training camp, Knueppel played six minutes before returning to the locker room during the first quarter. The Hornets have said the injury is left leg soreness, which is concerning, even though they didn’t mention the hamstring specifically. Sion James would be the likely replacement in the starting lineup if Knueppel misses time. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) has been upgraded to available to play against the Nets on Wednesday. 
 Knueppel missed the first eight games of the season, but he’ll be able to suit up against Brooklyn. It’s worth noting that Coby White (calf) made his season debut in Charlotte’s last game and played 16 minutes as a starter. The lopsided score could have been a factor, but the expectation should be that Knueppel replaces Sion James as a starter, though he likely plays a small role in this game. Grayson Allen will likely lose out on minutes with Knueppel back.

 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) is probable for Wednesday’s game against the Nets. 
 Based on the probable tag, Knueppel’s season debut is approaching. If he can play Wednesday, Sion James may head to the bench, even if the Hornets limit Knueppel’s minutes. Despite his own minutes restriction, Coby White started his season debut on Monday against the Pistons and played 16 minutes.

 CHA

 #7 
 Kon Knueppel (hamstring) is out for Monday’s game against the Pistons. 
 While Knueppel is close to making his season debut, he isn’t ready yet. Sion James is likely to remain in the starting lineup until last season’s Rookie of the Year runner-up is cleared to play without restrictions. 
 Dennis Schröder 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #17 
 Dennis Schröder (foot) is questionable to play against the Wizards on Friday. 
 Schröder has been the starter with Coby White (calf) sidelined to start the year. If Schröder is unavailable, Sion James will likely take over point guard duties, with Grayson Allen entering the starting unit. Rookie Christian Anderson Jr. would also likely take on extra minutes off the bench, and there is a slight chance he starts. 
 Kon Knueppel 
 CHA 
 Guard-Forward 
 #7 
 Kon Kneuppel (hamstring) is out for Monday’s game against the Wizards. 
 As of October 20, Knueppel, who had missed the entire preseason with a hamstring strain, had resumed on-court work. However, he still has not reached the point where he can play in games. While Sion James has started Charlotte’s first three games, Grayson Allen is the better option for fantasy managers looking for a streamer. 
 Sion James 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #4 
 The Charlotte Hornets will start Dennis Schroeder, Sion James, Brandon Miller, Naz Reid, and Moussa Diabate against the the Hawks on Friday. 
 Despite Grayson Allen having a real good game on Wednesday, Sion James is still the starter for this game. Given that Sion did start 19 games last year, it seems like he will stay in the starting lineup until players return to help balance out the starters. Grayson Allen can still be rostered in some spots until players start getting back, but he’ll be a streamer in most cases. 
 Grayson Allen 
 CHA 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Grayson Allen had 21 points (6-of-9 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and five three-pointers against the Nets on Wednesday. 
 With Kon Knueppel (hamstring) sidelined, the Hornets need Sion James and Allen to pick up the slack. James started, but scored just three points in 26 minutes. Meanwhile, Allen had 21 points and five three-pointers in 28 minutes off the bench. Allen is the preferred streaming option while Knueppel is sidelined.

 Anthony Davis erupted for a season-high 44 points (16-of-21 FGs, 10-of-11 FTs), 13 rebounds, one assist and one steal over 34 minutes as the Wizards fell to the Pistons 122-111 on Monday.
 Davis was nearly unstoppable in the opening half, connecting on 10-of-11 shots from the floor and all eight of his nine free-throw attempts to pour in a staggering 30 points. It was the highest-scoring first half by any player in the league this season, surpassing Victor Wembanyama’s 29-point outburst earlier this month. He accounted for more than half of Washington’s 58 first-half points in his return from a three-game absence due to a sprained ankle. Clearly, he’s feeling fine from a physical standpoint. Unfortunately, it wasn’t enough to power the Wizards to a win as they committed a staggering 18 turnovers in a losing effort.
 -  George Bissell

 John Collins 
 DET 
 Forward-Center 
 #20 
 Player Stats
 Link copied to clipboard! 
 John Collins delivered a season-high 24 points (9-of-13 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block across 28 minutes in Monday’s win over the Wizards.
 Collins went to work early on against Washington’s inexperienced front court, exploiting them for 15 first-half points. He added nine more after the break to cross the 20-point threshold for the first time since a 23-point effort against the Heat back on October 23. He’s done a nice job ostensibly replacing the Tobias Harris role for Detroit, but his scoring upside is rather limited in a supporting role. The Pistons took care of business on the second night of a back-to-back and will receive a couple days off before a rematch against the Wizards on Thursday.
 -  George Bissell

 AJ Dybantsa

 Forward 
 #4 
 Player Stats

 AJ Dybantsa poured in 21 points (8-of-17 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), eight rebounds, one assist and two blocks over 37 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Pistons.
 Dybantsa continues to show flashes of immense fantasy potential, but it’s abundantly clear that he’s a work in progress while acclimating to everyday life at the highest level. The 19-year-old phenom’s most impressive bucket of the night came early in the second quarter when he shook John Collins with a fake eurostep before flying to the rim for a two-hand slam. He’s tallied at least 17 point in five of seven games since making his season debut back on October 28.
 -  George Bissell

 Cade Cunningham

 Guard

 Cade Cunningham posted 17 points (7-of-16 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists and one steal over 27 minutes in Monday’s win over the Wizards.
 Cunningham turned in his second consecutive lackluster shooting performance, going 0-for-4 from three-point range while attempting 16 shots or fewer for just the fourth time this season. He poured in 11 first-half points and played a season-low 27 minutes during the second game of a back-to-back for Detroit. This looks like a relatively minor blip on the radar as he works through a shooting slump. He’ll get a couple days off before the Pistons square off with the Wizards in a rematch on Thursday.
 -  George Bissell

 Luka Dončić

 Luka Dončić accumulated 32 points (11-of-22 FGs, 7-of-7 FTs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, five steals and two blocks over 39 minutes to lead the Lakers to a 124-114 win over the Hawks on Monday.
 Dončić fell short of the 40-point plateau in his return from a one-game absence due to a minor back issue, but showed no signs of rust, turning in another spectacular all-around performance that left him two rebounds shy of a triple-double. He scored 18 of his 32 points after halftime, helping Los Angeles withstand a late Atlanta rally before pulling away in the closing minutes. The Lakers were also without Austin Reaves (illness) in this one, making Dončić’s latest all-around performance even more impressive. The 27-year-old franchise cornerstone has been virtually unstoppable through the early stages of the season and has quickly established himself as the frontrunner in the MVP race.
 -  George Bissell

 Onyeka Okongwu posted 16 points (6-of-11 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists and one steal over 30 minutes in Monday’s loss to the Lakers.
 Okongwu was one of the bright spots for Atlanta in this one as he got off to an excellent start, knocking down a pair of three-pointers as part of a nine-point outburst in the opening stanza. He’s reached double-digit points in five consecutive games since the start of November and is averaging over 16 points and nine rebounds during that span. The Hawks will attempt to get back on track when the face the Bulls in a road matchup on Friday.

 Walker Kessler delivered 21 points (8-of-12 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), 10 rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block over 30 minutes in Monday’s win over the Hawks.
 Kessler got off to an outstanding start with 15 first-half points and he managed to pull down just enough rebounds to notch a double-double for the seventh consecutive game since late October. The 25-year-old big man has fit seamlessly into Los Angeles’ nucleus after missing nearly all of last season following shoulder surgery.

 Alexander-Walker has been a consistent scoring threat for fantasy managers, scoring at least 20 points on eight occasions this season. He’s accomplished the feat in seven of his last eight games since October 28. He would’ve had an even bigger scoring performance had he not gone just 4-of-14 from three-point range in this one. The Hawks are back in action with a road matchup against the Bulls on Friday.
